Hi Rachel / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. LaunchForge is finalizing sponsor packages for our Fall cohort and we have two operational questions where we need Redwood's input before we finalize terms with our sponsors: 

1) Sponsor bucketing: one sponsor wants their $50k package split across 3 startups (not seats). Can Redwood allocate sponsor credits across multiple accounts under one sponsor umbrella, and can we set per-startup ceilings so unused dollars automatically roll back to the sponsor pool at quarter-end?

2) Trial pack composition: we usually provide a 60k token sandbox + 10k dedicated credit as the default sponsor pack. Is there flexibility to convert some sandbox tokens into pre-provisioned Dedicated credits for high-CPU inference (e.g., 8k quantized tokens -> reserved capacity hours) without changing the price band?

I've attached the sponsor tiers and a tentative mutual-action plan for redlines. Can you confirm feasibility and any operational or billing impacts? Also copying Tom from VentureBridge who may want to weigh in on billing flow.

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. Short answer: yes to both, with a couple of constraints and one recommended pattern. High level:

- Sponsor bucketing: Redwood supports a "sponsor umbrella" construct that lets a sponsor own a single credit pool and create child allocations to startup accounts. You can set per-child ceilings and an expiration/rollback policy. Operational notes: rollbacks are processed nightly and can be configured to be immediate or at quarter boundaries. Rollback to sponsor pool is supported but we recommend a small grace window (48–72 hours) to account for asynchronous usage spikes.

- Converting sandbox tokens to Dedicated credits: we can issue Dedicated-hours reservations out of sponsor pools, but there are two tradeoffs to call out: (1) Dedicated reservations consume capacity and may require a short-term reservation fee depending on the cohort dates; (2) Dedicated-hour vs token accounting needs an internal conversion rate (we use PCC: provisioned compute credit) because dedicated usage is billed by GPU-hour rather than token. We can absorb that conversion without changing the published sponsor price band if you accept a small carveout: a 5% provisioning fee on reserved hours to account for scheduling and capacity hold.

Next steps I suggest: 1) we draft the sponsor umbrella config in the MA (I can propose language), 2) Ben will outline the billing flow (separate email below) that shows invoice lines for sponsor pool draw, child allocations, and any provisioning fees, and 3) Priyom will check partner-facing product UX for creating these child allocations.

I put proposed contract language in the attached (see page 2 of the MA plan).

—Rachel

Alyssa / Rachel — quick operational breakdown on billing lines so your finance team can preview: 

1) Sponsor Pool (invoiceable line item): sponsor pays upfront or via net-30. Pool drawdown appears as a net usage credit on the sponsor's bill and as negative usage on startups' bills (i.e., covered by sponsor).

2) Child allocations (reporting): startups get their own monthly statement showing usage and remaining allocation; these are not invoiceable if covered by sponsor pool. If a startup exceeds its ceiling, we auto-charge overage back to the sponsor unless you opt into direct startup billing for that account.

3) Dedicated reservation fee (if used): separate line on sponsor invoice for reservation fee (if sponsor converts sandbox tokens into reserved Dedicated hours). We can waive this fee for first-time sponsors on cohorts <= 6 weeks with a signed commitment.

4) Rollback & reconciliation: rollbacks show as credit transfers rather than refunds. Quarterly reconciliations can be exported as a CSV (we can include a sample export).

If you want, I can put sample invoice mockups in a follow-up. From our side, everything Rachel noted is feasible. Happy to sync on Thursday if you'd like to run numbers.

—Ben
